scorecards.inningsCommentary: Entering the third innings with the match balance in flux, West Indies sought to extend their lead and set a decisive fourth-innings target. KC Brathwaite anchored the innings with a resolute 40, providing backbone against a probing bowling attack while middle-order partnerships consolidated the position. England's bowling response was spearheaded by Stuart Broad (3/34), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. West Indies's total of 137/10 (45.4 ov) closed their second innings, cementing a formidable target and transferring immense pressure onto the opposition.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Edgbaston commenced with high tactical intensity as England posted 514/8 (135.5 ov) in their opening innings. In response, West Indies countered with 168/10 (46.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: AN Cook 243 (408b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, AN Cook delivered a masterclass for England (243 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (England 64%) and allowing England to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, West Indies faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. England's bowling unit, bolstered by Joe Root (136 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing England won by innings & 209 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: England's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While West Indies produced fighting phases, England won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
